name: Xiamen
operatingHours: Xiamen Metro runs ~6:00 AM–~11:00 PM daily (first trains ~5:30–6:00 AM, last trains from the city ~10:30–11:00 PM; varies by line and station). Trains every 3–5 min at peak, 5–10 min off-peak. Lines 4 and 6 opened for trial service in September 2026 with shorter hours. No all-night service.
fareInfo: Distance-based single fares from ¥2 up to ~¥8 (2026). Pay with cash at ticket machines for a single-journey ticket, or scan the Alipay/WeChat transit QR code (厦门乘车码) at the gates; foreign Visa/Mastercard cards can be linked to Alipay or WeChat Pay. An E-Tong (Xiamen e-Pass) stored-value card also works on metro, BRT and buses. Gulangyu ferries are ticketed separately.

hotels.note: About 1.5 km from Terminal 3; the hotel runs a free 24-hour airport shuttle (3–5 min to T3, 10–15 min to T4).

sights.name: Gulangyu Island (Kulangsu)
sights.note: A car-free, UNESCO-listed island of colonial villas, piano houses and banyan-shaded lanes a short ferry ride from downtown; visitors sail from the Xiamen International Cruise Center (Dongdu), not the residents' ferry by Zhongshan Road.
sights.hours: Island open all day; visitor ferries ~7:00 AM–~6:00 PM, returns until late evening

sights.name: Zhongshan Road Pedestrian Street
sights.note: Xiamen's arcaded old shopping street running down to the waterfront, lined with qilou shophouses and stalls selling peanut soup, oyster omelettes and pia pia cakes; busiest and prettiest after dark.
sights.hours: Open all day; shops ~10:00 AM–10:00 PM

sights.name: Nanputuo Temple
sights.note: A large working Buddhist temple at the foot of Wulao Peak beside Xiamen University, with incense-filled halls and hillside paths up to rock carvings and city views; entry is free.

sights.name: Xiamen Botanical Garden (Wanshi Mountain)
sights.note: A hilly garden in the middle of the island with a rainforest valley, cactus and succulent houses and misty bamboo groves; paths link down towards Nanputuo Temple.

sights.name: Xiamen University
sights.note: One of China's most attractive campuses, with red-roofed 'Jiageng-style' buildings around a lotus lake by the sea; visitor entry needs a free advance reservation (passport accepted) and daily quotas fill up.
sights.hours: Visitor slots usually ~12:00–2:00 PM on weekdays and longer at weekends/holidays; closed to visitors at some times

sights.name: Shuzhuang Garden
sights.note: A seaside garden on Gulangyu's south shore with a zig-zag bridge over the water and the Piano Museum inside, built by a Taiwanese gentry family in the 1910s.

sights.name: Sunlight Rock (Riguang Yan)
sights.note: The granite summit in the middle of Gulangyu and the island's highest point, reached by stone steps for a panorama over the red roofs and across to Xiamen's skyline.

sights.name: Jimei School Village
sights.note: The waterfront campus built by overseas-Chinese philanthropist Tan Kah Kee, with swallow-tail roofed school buildings, his memorial museum and the carved stone Turtle Garden (Aoyuan); on the mainland, reached by Metro Line 1 to Jimei School Village station and a 20-min walk.
sights.hours: Campus grounds open all day; Turtle Garden and museum ~8:30 AM–5:30 PM (museum closed Mon)

sights.name: Baicheng Beach
sights.note: A public sandy beach just south of Xiamen University with views across to the Taiwanese-held Kinmen islands, the start of the Huandao Road seaside cycle path.

sights.name: Hulishan Fortress
sights.note: A late-Qing coastal battery on a headland east of Baicheng Beach, home to a 19th-century Krupp cannon and a small museum, with sea views towards Kinmen.

sights.name: Zengcuo'an Village
sights.note: A former fishing village off Huandao Road turned into a maze of narrow alleys full of snack stalls, cafés and guesthouses; crowded but fun for street food in the evening.
sights.hours: Open all day; stalls ~10:00 AM–10:00 PM

sights.name: Overseas Chinese Museum
sights.note: A free museum founded by Tan Kah Kee telling the story of Fujianese emigrants to Southeast Asia and beyond, with photos, objects and recreated streets.

sights.name: Haiwan Park
sights.note: A seaside lawn and promenade on the west shore of the island, good for a sunset walk looking across the harbour to Gulangyu and Haicang.

sights.name: Bailuzhou Park
sights.note: A park on an island in Yundang Lake with egret sculptures, lawns and evening fountain shows, surrounded by the city's business district.

sights.name: Wuyuanwan Wetland Park
sights.note: Xiamen's largest wetland park, with boardwalks and bridges over tidal lagoons on the island's north-east shore; next to Metro Line 2 Wetland Park station.

sights.name: Eighth Market (Badashi)
sights.note: A crowded old wet market near the north end of Zhongshan Road where locals buy live seafood and dried fish, with snack stalls cooking up oyster omelettes and fish balls; come in the morning.
sights.hours: ~6:00 AM–~1:00 PM best; some stalls into the afternoon

railStations.name: Xiamen North Railway Station
railStations.note: Xiamen's main high-speed rail hub in Jimei on the mainland, ~20 km north of the island centre: G/D trains to Fuzhou, Shenzhen, Shanghai, Beijing and beyond. Metro Line 1 (terminus area) runs to Zhongshan Road/Zhenhai Road in ~50 min.

railStations.name: Xiamen Railway Station
railStations.note: The central station on Xiamen Island next to the MixC mall: many high-speed and conventional trains along the coast terminate here. Metro Line 3 starts underneath, and Line 1 (Hubin East Road) is a short walk; Zhongshan Road is ~15 min by taxi.
railStations.hours: Trains ~6:00 AM–~11:00 PM to individual timetables; Line 3 ~6:00 AM–~11:00 PM.

airports.name: Xiamen Gaoqi International Airport
airports.transitNote: About 10 km north of Zhongshan Road on Xiamen Island. No metro station at the terminals: T3 (international and XiamenAir) and T4 (other domestic airlines) are 3–4 km apart, with a free shuttle between them. BRT from T4 and airport buses run to the city (40–60 min); a taxi to Zhongshan Road is ~¥35–50 and 20–30 min. Gaoqi is due to close when the new Xiamen Xiang'an International Airport opens (planned ~late December 2026); check which airport your flight uses.
airports.hours: Terminals follow the flight schedule; airport buses and BRT run ~6:00 AM–~10:00 PM, taxis for later arrivals.
